title: Conservation Laws for Modern Neural Architectures
claim: The level set of a simple conserved quantity can be disconnected, so conservation does not confine trajectories to one connected component.
layout: single panel contour plot, saddle geometry, colorbar-free, labeled level curves
description: A single filled contour plot of the function a^2 - b^2 over axes a (horizontal, about -3.5 to 3.5) and b (vertical, about -2.5 to 2.5), titled 'a^2 - b^2 = c'. The surface is a saddle. Labeled contour lines run from -5 at the top and bottom, where they are dashed, to 11 at the left and right edges, where they are solid. The Spectral colormap goes from red at negative values (top and bottom) through pale orange and yellow near zero to green and blue at large positive values (left and right). Two straight lines cross at the origin and form an X. This is the c = 0 level set. Positive level sets form separate hyperbola branches on the left and right. Negative level sets form separate branches above and below. The eye goes first to the X at the center, then to the separated branches.
caption: The disconnectedness of the level set {a2 −b2 = c}.
abstract: Understanding gradient descent dynamics is key to explaining the success of over-parameterized models, where implicit bias manifests through conservation laws in gradient flow. While such laws are well understood for linear and ReLU networks, they remain largely unexplored for modern architectures. This work develops a unified framework to characterize conservation laws for contemporary models, including feedforward networks with GELU, SiLU, and SwiGLU activations, multihead attention with sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings, and Mixture-of-Experts architectures under diverse gating designs. Our theoretical findings are supported by experiments that validate the predicted invariants.
